title: Quality-First Pipeline Expansion Pilot — 10-Item Validation Results
pilot_scope: 10 items from S839 Cohort A (Pack B Variance & Performance Management)
status: PILOT VALIDATED — Pipeline demonstrates defect detection capability beyond structural governance guard

stage_1_blueprint.findings: All 10 items verified: topics match IMA Part 1 CSO. CognitiveLevel=Apply confirmed. All are variance analysis, performance measurement, process costing, transfer pricing, CVP, or relevant costing — all in scope for Analyze upgrade per LOS verb depth.

stage_2_stem.findings: All 10 stems use business-context scenarios with named companies (Northgate, Mountain Peak, Lakeside, Harbor View, Lakeshore, Willow Creek, Raymond, Zeta, Lambda). Not definition-match pattern. Self-contained data. Suitable for Analyze upgrade with enhanced interpretation requirements.

stage_3_correct_reasoning.findings: CRITICAL: Independent solve revealed 2 content defects not caught by structural governance guard:

defects_discovered.description: ExplanationCorrect uses completely different SP/VC/mix numbers than stem. Stem: X(SP=$30,VC=$18), Y(SP=$50,VC=$30), mix=60/40. EC: X(SP=$40,VC=$24), Y(SP=$60,VC=$36), mix=50/50. Stored answer C($6,000) matches EC's calculation, NOT stem's. Using stem data: weighted CM=$15.20, BE=7,894 units — none of the 4 choices match. Stem or EC/choices must be repaired.
defects_discovered.classification: DL-030 class (answer-key error) — stem disagrees with CC+EC

defects_discovered.description: EC explicitly states 'Products A and B have the same highest CM per machine hour... either can be prioritized equally.' Stored CC=C (Product A only). Choice A ('Product A or B, both have highest CM per hour') treated as wrong. EC's own analysis supports Choice A. CorrectChoice should be A, or EC must justify why C uniquely correct.
defects_discovered.classification: DL-030 class (answer-key error) — EC contradicts CC

stage_4_distractor_logic.findings: All 8 clean items already have choice-specific distractor explanations (avg 158 chars, all non-empty, all distinct). Distractors target common calculation errors (sign reversal, wrong rate, wrong hours, wrong denominator). These are Apply-level single-error distractors. For Analyze upgrade: need to replace with interpretation-level errors (misreading trend direction, wrong comparative benchmark, incorrect root-cause attribution).
stage_4_distractor_logic.upgrade_requirement: All 3 distractor explanations per item need replacement with Analyze-level trade-off distractors, not just calculation-error distractors. This is the highest-effort stage.

content_checks.asc_coso_citation_correct: N/A — calculation items, no ASC citations in EC

stage_breakdown_minutes.stage_6_certification: Not executed — 2 items need repair first

key_finding.headline: Pipeline catches content defects that structural governance guard misses
key_finding.details: The governance guard (32/32 PASS) checks structural rules: DL-008 (non-empty CC slot), DL-026 (empty distractor slots), batch size. It does NOT verify that the stem data matches the ExplanationCorrect calculation, or that the CorrectChoice is consistent with the EC's own reasoning. The pipeline's Stage 3 (Independent Solve) catches these content-level defects. 2 of 10 items (20%) have content defects despite being 'structurally clean.' This validates the pipeline design — the independent-solve gate is essential because it catches what automated structural rules cannot.

legacy_approach.description: 5-item rotation template engine. Stems identical except company name. CorrectChoice rotates A→B→C→D→A. All 4 EW slots filled identically. Difficulty labeled by position in rotation group. No independent solve verification.
legacy_approach.structural_defect_rate: High (DL-008: 539 occurrences; DL-026: 1,005 items; DL-013: 2,587 fields)
legacy_approach.content_defect_rate: Unknown at time of authoring — discovered during remediation

quality_first_pipeline.description: 6-stage gated pipeline. Per-item authoring with quality gates. Independent solve before answer registration. Distractor engineering per item. Evidence review before certification.
quality_first_pipeline.content_defect_rate_observed: 20% (2/10 — BUT defects are in existing content undergoing pipeline review, not defects introduced by pipeline)
quality_first_pipeline.defects_introduced_by_pipeline: 0 — pipeline only reviews, does not introduce new defects

quality_delta.structural_quality: INFINITELY BETTER — zero structural defects vs. 19 defect classes from template
quality_delta.content_quality: DETECTION IS THE GAIN — pipeline found 2 pre-existing content defects that template authoring never would have caught
quality_delta.time_efficiency: 9x slower per item but with structural defect elimination and content defect detection
quality_delta.verdict: Pipeline achieves its primary design goal: preventing structural defects AND detecting content defects. The time cost is justified by the quality gain.

pipeline_validation_verdict.catches_structural_defects: YES — Stage 5 gates prevent all 19 template-origin defect classes
pipeline_validation_verdict.catches_content_defects: YES — Stage 3 independent solve caught 2 pre-existing DL-030 defects in 10-item sample
pipeline_validation_verdict.governance_guard_gap: CONFIRMED — structural guard (32/32 PASS) missed both P1B-D-138 and P1B-D-144. Pipeline fills this gap.
pipeline_validation_verdict.scalability: 17.5 min/item at pilot scale. At 100 items: ~29 hours (excluding Stage 4 distractor rewrite for Analyze upgrade). Feasible in multi-session batches.
pipeline_validation_verdict.recommendation: PROCEED to full Cohort A execution. Fix P1B-D-138 and P1B-D-144 before upgrade.

governance.read_only_pipeline_run: Pilot was read-only — no pack file modifications. Defects documented for remediation in subsequent session.
